gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Xbox model has to be the Arctis Nova 5X specifically. SteelSeries says the Nova 5 and Nova 5P won't work with Xbox, even with a separately bought Nova 5X dongle. Even on the 5X, the dongle's switch has to be set to 'Xbox' for an Xbox Series X|S or Xbox One and to 'USB' for PC or PlayStation.
standout_why: I compared against three pages. SoundGuys, which ChatGPT cited, says only that the Nova 5X can 'seamlessly connect to Xbox, PlayStation, Switch, PC, and mobile devices' and mentions a 'USB-C dongle with a platform switch'. It never mentions the Nova 5 or 5P, never says they lack Xbox, and never says a 5X dongle can't fix that. RTINGS' best-gaming page lists the suffixes '[7, 7P, 7X]' for the Nova 7 without saying what they mean. The GamesRadar page ChatGPT cited returned only its title, with the body cut off, so I couldn't check it. ChatGPT's own answer said '5X … Works with PC, Xbox, PS5 and Switch' but didn't warn that the similar-looking Nova 5 and 5P SKUs (SteelSeries' arctis-nova-5x URL even opens the 'Arctis Nova 5 Wireless' page, which doesn't list Xbox) shut out Xbox for good.
decides: For someone who owns an Xbox, or might, this confirms ChatGPT's wireless pick only for the exact SKU 'Arctis Nova 5X'. A Nova 5 or 5P, often listed next to it, can't be made to work with Xbox, so the SKU letter decides what to buy. The same kind of split shows up at HyperX: the Cloud III Wired ($57.99) lists Xbox Series X|S and Xbox One, but the Cloud III Wireless ($149.99) lists only PC, PS5 and Nintendo Switch. So for a PC + Xbox shopper on a budget, the wired Cloud III is the safe pick. EKSA's own store also says Xbox doesn't work on either wireless mode of its E900WT, which matters for Dealectric's EKSA wireless listings.
